description:
The Query Workbench is functional, but the retheme audit found that it still
looks and behaves like an internal debugging tool. Desktop prioritizes
`Visible Columns` above the result table, filters use plain white cards and
native checkboxes, the mobile drawer is a default full-screen list, and the
advanced SQL surface competes with the primary browse workflow. The page also
inherits inconsistent button, table, card, chip, and form styling.

This item should preserve the power-user capability while making the default
experience understandable for public users who want to filter, inspect, and
export result bundles.

anti_patterns.dont: break mobile drawer focus trapping while retheming the filters.
make every column visible by default to avoid designing the column controls.
remove SQL/export power features; make them subordinate to the primary workflow.
turn Query Workbench into a marketing explainer page; it is a tool surface.

preserves.behavior: CSV and JSON export output exactly the user-visible selected columns.
Hidden `result_id` remains available for row View links.
SQL scratchpad remains read-only against the browser snapshot.

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run test:e2e:fixtures && npm run build && npx playwright test --project=chromium --grep query
echo 'Manual: capture /results/query at 390, 768, 1280, 1600; test filters drawer, exports, visible columns, SQL, row action, and table overflow'

work_units.notes:
Outcome: narrowed this PR to a token/accessibility migration rather than
reopening the Query Workbench workflow. The primary path remains result
count, filters, result rows, row limit, and export. Advanced SQL remains
in its existing collapsed disclosure. The deeper split that would move
Visible Columns and Build SQL From Filters behind an advanced affordance
is deferred to a product/UX follow-up, not claimed as delivered here.
work_units.summary: Define the public Query Workbench workflow and advanced-only controls

work_units.notes:
Outcome: query header, summary toolbar, row-limit control, and export
buttons were migrated to surface/focus tokens. The row-limit control keeps
its existing compact two-button behavior and now uses tokenized selected
state.
work_units.summary: Retheme the query header, summary toolbar, row-limit control, and exports

work_units.notes:
Outcome: `FacetRail`/`FacetDrawer` were tokenized and continue to use the
existing focus trap, escape handling, reset affordance, count labels, and
active chip preview. The broader filter information-architecture redesign
is deferred; this PR does not claim a new filter model.

Outcome: Visible Columns styling was tokenized while preserving schema-
driven column state and export behavior. Relocating it below the table,
into a disclosure, or into a configuration popover is deferred to the
advanced/primary workflow follow-up.

Outcome: result and SQL tables were migrated to data-surface tokens while
preserving existing schema-driven rendering, sorting, and row actions.
This follow-up adds the shared `.bb-scroll-affordance` cue to the query
result and SQL tables at narrow widths.
work_units.summary: Retheme result and SQL tables with consistent formatting

work_units.notes:
Outcome: Advanced SQL remains collapsed by default and was migrated to the
same token language as the rest of the page. SQL errors now render with
`role="alert"` so tests and assistive technology depend on semantics, not
legacy color classes.
work_units.summary: Retheme Advanced SQL and starter queries

work_units.notes:
Outcome: targeted unit and browser checks cover facet URL round trip,
row-limit mode, visible-column rendering, CSV/JSON export, SQL read-only
errors, and the preserved mobile drawer focus trap. Manual end-to-end
responsive redesign remains deferred with the UX follow-up above.
work_units.summary: Verify URL state, export behavior, mobile drawer, and keyboard paths
